To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the variance of the autosomal fraction of admixture in an admixed population is informative about sex-biased introgression from a contributing source group and the variance decreases as the bias increases.

the variance of autosomes in admixed populations is informative about sex-biased gene flow, and that the long-term variance of autosomal DNA decreases as the sex-biased contribution from a source population increases.
sex bias in admixture is informative in the autosomal variance, but not in the autosomal mean.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of sex-biases in the admixture process on the autosomal genetic variation in admixed populations.
the development and application of a model that mechanizes sex-specific admixture processes and enables inference about the history of admixture.
the effect of complex admixture processes on the autosomal DNA of admixed populations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the variance of admixture is a better indicator of sex bias in admixture processes than the mean.
the variance of autosomes can provide evidence about the sex bias of admixture in a population.
sex-biased gene flow can be informative about the sex-bias in admixture history, but only if the autosomal and sex-linked variation are considered simultaneously.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the autosomal admixure fraction is a useful summary of the history of sex-biase admixture.
the variance in autosomal admixture from a specific source is informative about sex-biased contributions from that source.
the autosomal admixed population is a poor indicator for sex bias in admixture history.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the variance of autosomally derived admixture levels can be used to infer sex bias in admixture histories.
the autosomal admixed variance can be informative about the history of sex-biassed admixture.
, in the long term, the variance of the autosomal fraction is informative about sex-biased introgression.
